verses.text: These are the names of the sons of Israel who went to Egypt with Jacob, each one with his family:
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
Jacob's family who came from him numbered seventy people in all. Joseph was already in Egypt.
Then Joseph died, and so did all his brothers and all the people of that time.
But the people of Israel had many children. Their numbers grew and grew, and they became very strong. The land was filled with them.
Then a new king came to power in Egypt, who did not know about Joseph.
He said to his people, "Look, the people of Israel are more in number and stronger than we are.
Come, we must deal with them wisely, or they will grow even more. If war breaks out, they could join our enemies, fight against us, and leave the land."
So the Egyptians put slave masters over them to make their lives hard with heavy work. They built the store cities of Pithom and Raamses for Pharaoh.
But the more the Egyptians made them suffer, the more they grew in number and spread out. So the Egyptians came to fear the people of Israel.
The Egyptians forced the people of Israel to work without mercy.
They made their lives bitter with hard work, making mortar and bricks, and doing all kinds of work in the fields. In all their work, the Egyptians showed them no mercy.
Then the king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, the women who helped mothers give birth. One was named Shiphrah and the other Puah.
He said, "When you help the Hebrew women give birth and see them on the birthing stool, if the baby is a boy, kill him. But if it is a girl, let her live."
But the midwives feared God. They did not do what the king of Egypt told them. They let the baby boys live.
So the king of Egypt called for the midwives and asked them, "Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?"
The midwives answered Pharaoh, "The Hebrew women are not like Egyptian women. They are strong, and they give birth before the midwife gets there."
So God was good to the midwives, and the people kept growing in number and became very strong.
And because the midwives feared God, he gave them families of their own.
Then Pharaoh gave this order to all his people: "Every Hebrew boy that is born, you must throw into the River Nile. But let every girl live."
